\chapter{Preguntó Si --- A Question That Stops Being One}
\label{ch:pregunto-si}
\hlchaptermodality{214}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can report a yes-or-no question somebody asked.}

I can report a yes-or-no question somebody asked.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[preguntó si]{preguntó si}

\label{lesson:ES-C57-pregunto-si}



\begin{quote}
Report a statement. (\emph{Dijo que trabajaba}.)

Now the past of \emph{preguntar}, which is perfectly ordinary. (\emph{Preguntó}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a question, reported}]
\begin{quote}
\emph{¿Trabaja?} — the question, as asked. \emph{\textbf{Preguntó si trabajaba.}} — the question, reported.
\end{quote}

Two things changed, and both are worth naming.

\textbf{The joint is \emph{si}, not \emph{que}.} A statement goes in on \emph{que}; a yes-or-no question goes in on \emph{si}. The verb still steps back into the imperfect, exactly as before — that part has not changed at all.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
\textbf{And the question marks are gone.} Not forgotten — \emph{not allowed}. Look at what the reported sentence actually does: it tells you something. It is a statement about an act of asking, and nobody is being asked anything. The marks belong to a question being put, and no question is being put here.

So \emph{¿Preguntó si trabajaba?} is a real sentence, but it means something else — it asks whether he asked.

Now the \emph{si} itself. It is the same \emph{si} that opens a condition, and that is not a coincidence dressed up as one. Both uses hold something open that has not been settled: \emph{si tengo tiempo} leaves the time unsettled, \emph{si trabajaba} leaves the answer unsettled. English splits the job between \emph{whether} and \emph{if}. Spanish never needed to.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Preguntó si trabajaba}
  \item the question as asked, then the report
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which word joins a reported yes-or-no question? (\emph{\textbf{Si}}.)

And what happened to the question marks? (They \textbf{went}, because the sentence no longer asks anything.)
\end{tcolorbox}
